{{recipe}}

These attractive green '''spinach and ricotta gnocchi''' originated in Tuscany where, confusingly, they were known as ravioli.

==Ingredients==
* 12 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] cooked [[Cookbook:Spinach|spinach]], well drained and finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 1 container (8 oz) [[Cookbook:Ricotta|ricotta]], mashed until smooth
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]
* [[Cookbook:Nutmeg|Nutmeg]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Eggs|eggs]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] freshly-grated [[Cookbook:Parmesan Cheese|Parmesan cheese]]
* 3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* 5 tbsp [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], melted

==Procedure==
# Put the spinach, ricotta, and seasonings in a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]]. Cook gently, stirring continuously, for 5 minutes.
# Turn off the heat, then beat in the eggs, 3 tbsp of the Parmesan, and the flour to make a [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]].
# Chill the dough for at least 4 hours.
# Gently shape dough into small rounds and roll them in a very small amount of flour.
# [[Cookbook:Poaching|Poach]] them in boiling water until they float to the surface. Drain and set aside.
# [[Cookbook:Mixing#Tossing|Toss]] the gnocchi with melted butter, and top with remaining Parmesan cheese.
